import { z } from "zod";

const nonzeroId = /[1-9a-f]/;

const attribute = z.strictObject({
  key: z.string().max(256),
  value: z.strictObject({ stringValue: z.string().max(2048) }),
});

export const span = z.strictObject({
  side: z.enum(["server", "browser", "ssr", "worker"]),
  traceId: z
    .string()
    .regex(/^[0-9a-f]{32}$/)
    .refine((id) => nonzeroId.test(id)),
  spanId: z
    .string()
    .regex(/^[0-9a-f]{16}$/)
    .refine((id) => nonzeroId.test(id)),
  parentSpanId: z
    .string()
    .regex(/^[0-9a-f]{16}$/)
    .optional(),
  flags: z.literal(0).or(z.literal(1)),
  name: z.string().max(256),
  kind: z.literal(1),
  startTimeUnixNano: z.string().regex(/^\d{1,20}$/),
  endTimeUnixNano: z.string().regex(/^\d{1,20}$/),
  attributes: z.array(attribute).max(32),
  events: z
    .array(
      z.strictObject({
        name: z.string().max(256),
        timeUnixNano: z.string().regex(/^\d{1,20}$/),
        attributes: z.array(attribute).max(32),
      }),
    )
    .max(32),
  status: z.strictObject({
    code: z.literal(1).or(z.literal(2)),
    message: z.string().max(2048).optional(),
  }),
});

export const logRecord = z.strictObject({
  time: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
  level: z.number().int().min(10).max(60),
  msg: z.string().max(2048),
  service: z.string().min(1).max(128),
  side: z.enum(["server", "browser", "ssr", "worker"]),
  traceId: z
    .string()
    .regex(/^[0-9a-f]{32}$/)
    .optional(),
  spanId: z
    .string()
    .regex(/^[0-9a-f]{16}$/)
    .optional(),
  attributes: z.record(z.string().max(256), z.string().max(2048)).optional(),
});

export const telemetryBatch = z
  .strictObject({ traces: z.array(span).max(64), logs: z.array(logRecord).max(64) })
  .refine((batch) => batch.traces.length + batch.logs.length <= 64);

---
name: tinker-feature
description: Add a feature from its table to its page.
---

# Add one feature

Read the [current authoring contract](https://github.com/lagz0ne/tinker-app/blob/next/docs/decisions/start-decompose.md) for imports, ownership,
input checks, and commit-before-success. Use the board's issue operations as
the new session-transaction write example. Counter and todos use the same session transaction and owned call boundary;
their small write bodies are useful starting examples.

Read this path in order:

1. src/demo/backend/todos.schema.server.ts and src/demo/contracts/todos-contract.ts.
2. src/demo/backend/todos.server.ts and src/demo/backend/sync.server.ts.
3. src/transport/todos.functions.ts and src/demo/contracts/sync.ts.
4. src/demo/frontend/records.ts, src/frontend/Todos.tsx, and src/routes/todos.tsx.
5. tests/todos.test.ts and tests/presets.ts.

Add the schema to drizzle.config.ts and generate its migration. Take the actor
from currentUser rather than caller input. Keep execution replay guards, stream
lock order, saved changes, and events in one write transaction. A repeated
execution ID must not repeat saved effects. Run each shared step through a
controller so it has a span. The transport owns the child call and its signal.

Private page guards call context.account and context.bootstrap. They only read.
Keep drafts separate from saved data. Extend Register and the event reader
before adding a page. Views invoke operations and show checked results.

Run build, type checks, serial tests, schema, and the listed app gates.

---
name: tinker-forms
description: Choose the owner of new app code.
---

# Choose a form

Read the [current authoring contract](https://github.com/lagz0ne/tinker-app/blob/next/docs/decisions/start-decompose.md) first. It owns the rules for
forms, native boundaries, imports, settings, pure helpers, and the cap of 17.
Do not copy a second version of those rules into feature code.

Choose a tag for an injected value, data for visible state, a resource for an
owned client/private work state, or an operation for an action. The examples
are databaseUrl, profile/nameDraft, database/auth, and changeTodo. Counter and todo writes now use the session transaction; profile mail is the
remaining coupled migration.

For a new write, read database.transaction and the board's issues.change steps.
Resolve transaction only in write steps; reads keep database. A native call
owns the child session and joins its end before returning a reply.

Keep lazy outside-library resources in the owner's modules.ts. Use drizzleOrm
from the database public entry. Schemas and tables are declarations, not live
clients. A schema used once stays a schema. Validate raw input at the operation
boundary; use its result rather than a type cast.

Feature outgoing HTTP uses httpRequest.controller. Pass raw plain request
values; map status/body to a feature value or typed error. Tests replace
httpBackend through the HTTP public entry. Native Request/Response values
belong to routes, server functions, and the named auth mount.

Review `PLAIN.md` when keeping a pure helper. Run both plain checks after
changing its rules. The script is the full checked declaration/callback list.

---
name: tinker-seams
description: Keep wiring on the owner's public entries.
---

# Keep the seams

Read the [current authoring contract](https://github.com/lagz0ne/tinker-app/blob/next/docs/decisions/start-decompose.md) for the one-way imports,
required bindings, defineMain/exit, auth hooks, and copied-update policy.
Current Start commands are prepare, doctor, and serve. Add/update/check is
planned; it will stop on local edits and replace whole owned components.

Inspect the actual server, router, and start commands before changing wiring.
The command owns roots, config bindings, observers, and close order. Components
declare direct requires and use each other's public entries. A test may use
the private file it proves. Never forward a component through an app barrel
just to hide its owner.

Useful public entries:

- requests: startRequests, backendStop, requestStop; index.server has protocol state.
- database/index.server: database, transaction, databaseSetup, typed config, drizzleOrm.
- auth/index.server: auth settings, principal, liveAccount, and openSync.
- sync/index.server: eventHistory, account operations, notices, and server slots.
- sync: browser sync APIs, Register, reader slots, and recordsSlot.
- mail/index.server: mail, authMail, smtpUrl, mailFrom, and owned SMTP sockets.
- http/index.server: httpRequest; tests get httpBackend from http.

The stream implementation belongs to auth because it checks the live account.
Page bootstrap never creates stream rows. Signup/sign-in and the migration do.
Auth imports mandatory sync/mail work directly; there are no auth hook slots.

Follow src/routes/api.auth.$.ts and api.sync.ts for owned call dispatch. Bind
request values at that boundary. Host config and app/cross-root slots are
separate bindings. Follow the contract's checks after changing wiring.

---
name: tinker-sync
description: Choose mutations and sync for saved state.
---

# Saved changes and waits

Read the [current authoring contract](https://github.com/lagz0ne/tinker-app/blob/next/docs/decisions/start-decompose.md) for owned calls, auth,
stream creation, and transactions. Use sync for committed shared state; keep
drafts and view choices in data. Read-only page/bootstrap calls never write.

Read saveName in src/frontend/profile-actions.ts. It makes an execution ID with
ctx.random.uuid and registers sync.execute before sending the native server
function. Pass the native send function and its plain data record directly.
Do not wrap it in a signal-taking helper. Saved events update records; a final
result ends the wait. Do not patch saved records from a command receipt.

A lost reply retries the same execution ID. A separate mail retry uses a new
ID. Results distinguish a complete save, a saved value with failed required
mail work, and a failed save. The profile mail demo is a legacy flow; new board
mail uses an outbox row in the write transaction.

Sign-in holds reconnects with snapshotLoader.beginAccountChange, registers
endAccountChange in defer, leaves sync, then awaits completeAccountChange before
releasing the hold. Account exit cancels waits and ignores old replies.
The page shell's AuthSession keeps active logins fresh through explicit POST;
that does not move a write back into bootstrap.

Read src/demo/contracts/sync.ts for bodies and tests/sync.test.ts for the public
result. Stream/account checks use auth's public server entry.

---
name: tinker-testing
description: Prove app promises through small scopes.
---

# Test through a scope

Read the [current authoring contract](https://github.com/lagz0ne/tinker-app/blob/next/docs/decisions/start-decompose.md#http-and-tests) for the shared
check rules. Tests stay serial with VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 and
VP_RUN_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT=1. Never skip or quarantine a test.

Read tests/todos.test.ts, bootstrap-read.test.ts, transaction.test.ts, and
transaction-lease.test.ts. Tests bind typed tags and use native resource presets.
proofDatabase runs real PGlite queries; proofMail records sends. Tests may import
the private owner they prove. Never patch global fetch, clocks, or module state.
Use Core's test clock and resource presets at those native boundaries.

New write tests use the same owned call as a transport: a signal opens a child
session and joins defer before the result. Prove failed COMMIT, no early reply,
rollback, idle no-checkout, and ended handles. Do not mirror each internal step.
Keep command tests for input, startup, exit, and close; these are useful wiring
contracts. Native host proofs stay outside feature scope tests.

Old/expired-cookie page tests log all SQL writes. The browser refresh proof must
show an aged login renews through successful POST, rather than manually sending
the refresh from the test. A fault control must fail for its named cause.
Run the app's AGENTS.md gates and live proofs. Build before type checks/tests.

# Start authoring

Follow the parent repo's rules too. The [current contract](https://github.com/lagz0ne/tinker-app/blob/next/docs/decisions/start-decompose.md) owns the
full API, import, input, update, and helper rules. These five rules are its
local checklist; each release's changes stay in UPGRADE.md.

1. **Own the boundary.** Hosts own process inputs, sockets, OS stops, and output
   flush. Direct cmds files bind app inputs and own roots; scope tests own theirs.
   Keep wiring inline and test command input, startup, exit, and close.
2. **Keep imports one-way.** Base owns native entry/close/panic/observation glue.
   Components use public entries and direct requires, never base, app, or cmds.
   App code uses component public entries. Start ships tools and hosts.
3. **Declare work and owner.** Use tags, data, resources, and operations for their
   named jobs. Native bridges and extension hooks keep their owned contracts.
   No authored classes or live module clients. Pure helpers have at most three
   plain value inputs, at least two real callers, TSDoc, and a PLAIN.md entry.
   The cap stays **17**. Owned resource methods and native callbacks are not
   permission to pass a context bag through a plain helper.
4. **Bind only real seams.** Bind host config inline and validate startup values
   before ready. Bind request inputs per call. App readers, cross-root values,
   and native/test IO can use tags. Import mandatory component work directly.
   Not every required tag is startup config; defaults must support useful work.
5. **Close before success.** Use defineMain and the clean exit contract. Close
   app before telemetry and join the call before reply bytes or progress output.
   Board writes and the migrated counter/todos use the session transaction. New
   multi-step writes follow that pattern. Page reads write no tables; the browser

## Promises tested through app scopes

- Real accounts can sign up, sign in, sign out, and save a profile.
- Releasing mail makes a fresh sender.
- Releasing database makes a fresh handle.
- A bad stored event fails with StoredDataInvalid, a server failure, never a rejected change.
- A bad stored notification result has no retry available.
- Signed-out private writes open no transaction.
- Refused work leaves the server root usable.
- Failed transactions keep old data and publish no saved change.
- A native commit failure never returns a saved profile.
- Email check and reset callbacks use the declared mail action.
- Accounts can read and change only their own todos and event stream.
- Another account's todo ID cannot change or delete its row.
- Empty titles and caller-selected owners are refused.
- Concurrent public writes replay in commit order.
- Repeated execution IDs do not repeat saved effects.
- Events before receipts finish waits after saved records are applied.
- Replayed events and old snapshots keep newer records and drafts.
- Account exit stops waits and ignores late old responses.
- A private route check clears cached records after another tab signs out.
- Failed mail keeps the name and retry sends only mail.
- Committed profile work finishes after its request exits.
- Saved names stay readable while duplicate requests share a send.
- Commit wakes SSE; rollback publishes no wake.
- SSE replays saved events and refuses another account's cursor.
  A held SSE reader receives the next saved batch.
- A revoked session receives no queued private rows.
- A quiet private stream closes at the heartbeat after sign-out.
- A final result replay completes a wait after disconnect.
  The copied runtime tests cover request, HTTP, telemetry, and tab work.

## Limits

Event history has no retention rule yet.
SSE replays stored events; it is not a durable job queue.
A crash after commit can leave mail without a final result.
A crash after SMTP acceptance can cause a resend.
One send across several server processes is not promised.
SMTP acceptance means the server accepted mail.
Mailpit lets you see that message in local development.
Storage failure can drop records when its bounded queue fills.

## App HTTP rules

Use `httpRequest` from `~/components/http/index.server`.
Map its reply to a feature value or managed error.
Tests bind `httpBackend` from `~/components/http`.
App code may not use that tag or the raw `http` resource.

The plain check refuses built-in fetch, raw HTTP clients,
computed module loads, and createRequire in app code.
It refuses raw request headers outside the auth resource.
Replies belong to routes; operations take plain params.
Operations never take Request or return Response.
Native WebSocket and EventSource remain allowed.
Their resources own and close the connection.

## Durable mail worker

Auth callbacks await a saved mail row. Better Auth writes through its own pool
adapter, outside the session transaction, so auth enqueue is a separate call.
App writes can call enqueueMail in their own transaction. SMTP can deliver more
than once after acceptance followed by a lost acknowledgement.

Build and run the starter's worker beside its server:

```bash
npm run build:worker
npm run worker
```

Both await the same migration lock. The worker uses DATABASE_URL, SMTP_URL, and
SMTP_FROM from the local .env or host environment. It claims up to 20 rows, sends
outside locks, and saves results by lease token. OUTBOX_LEASE_MS defaults to
180000 and must be at least 120000. A send starts only while its send and ack
budgets fit in the remaining lease. Released unsent claims refund their attempt.
OUTBOX_SMTP_TIMEOUT_MS defaults to 3000 and may only shorten it.

Worker traces use side worker. Stdout and bounded history work without a
collector. To enable export, bind both VICTORIA_TRACES_URL and VICTORIA_LOGS_URL;
setting only one is a startup config error. OTEL_SERVICE_NAME defaults to
tinker-worker. Work closes before the existing bounded telemetry flush.

  const cases: [string, (raw: unknown) => unknown, unknown, boolean][] = [
    ["an execution", (raw) => readExecution.parse(raw), { executionId: id }, true],
    [
      "an execution id that is no UUID",
      (raw) => readExecution.parse(raw),
      { executionId: "1" },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "an execution with more keys",
      (raw) => readExecution.parse(raw),
      { executionId: id, extra: 1 },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "a retry",
      (raw) => readRetry.parse(raw),
      { executionId: id, previousExecutionId: other },
      true,
    ],
    [
      "a retry with no UUID",
      (raw) => readRetry.parse(raw),
      { executionId: id, previousExecutionId: "1" },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "a retry with more keys",
      (raw) => readRetry.parse(raw),
      { executionId: id, previousExecutionId: other, x: 1 },
      false,
    ],
    ["a cursor", (raw) => readCursor.parse(raw), { after: 0 }, true],
    ["a cursor below 0", (raw) => readCursor.parse(raw), { after: -1 }, false],
    ["a cursor between revisions", (raw) => readCursor.parse(raw), { after: 1.5 }, false],
    ["a cursor with more keys", (raw) => readCursor.parse(raw), { after: 1, x: 1 }, false],
    ["a private cursor", (raw) => readPrivateCursor.parse(raw), { accountId: "a", after: 3 }, true],
    [
      "a private cursor with no account",
      (raw) => readPrivateCursor.parse(raw),
      { accountId: "", after: 0 },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "a private cursor below 0",
      (raw) => readPrivateCursor.parse(raw),
      { accountId: "a", after: -1 },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "a private cursor with more keys",
      (raw) => readPrivateCursor.parse(raw),
      { accountId: "a", after: 0, x: 1 },
      false,
    ],
    ["an event", (raw) => eventEnvelope.parse(raw), event, true],
    [
      "a result event",
      (raw) => eventEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { ...event, payload: { kind: "result", result: "r" } },
      true,
    ],
    ["an event at revision 0", (raw) => eventEnvelope.parse(raw), { ...event, revision: 0 }, false],
    [
      "an event between revisions",
      (raw) => eventEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { ...event, revision: 1.5 },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "an event with no UUID",
      (raw) => eventEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { ...event, executionId: "1" },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "an event of another kind",
      (raw) => eventEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { ...event, payload: { kind: "other" } },
      false,
    ],
    ["an event with no stream", (raw) => eventEnvelope.parse(raw), { ...event, stream: 1 }, false],
    ["a snapshot", (raw) => snapshotEnvelope.parse(raw), snapshot, true],
    [
      "an account snapshot",
      (raw) => snapshotEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { ...snapshot, private: { stream: "a", revision: 2 } },
      true,
    ],
    [
      "a snapshot of another stream",
      (raw) => snapshotEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { ...snapshot, public: { stream: "a", revision: 0 } },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "a snapshot below 0",
      (raw) => snapshotEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { ...snapshot, public: { stream: "public", revision: -1 } },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "an account snapshot below 0",
      (raw) => snapshotEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { ...snapshot, private: { stream: "a", revision: -1 } },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "an account snapshot with no stream",
      (raw) => snapshotEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { ...snapshot, private: { revision: 0 } },
      false,
    ],
    ["a batch", (raw) => batchEnvelope.parse(raw), { version: 0, events: [event] }, true],
    [
      "a batch below version 0",
      (raw) => batchEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { version: -1, events: [] },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "a batch between versions",
      (raw) => batchEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { version: 0.5, events: [] },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "a batch with a broken event",
      (raw) => batchEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { version: 0, events: [{}] },
      false,
    ],
    ["a bootstrap", (raw) => bootstrapEnvelope.parse(raw), { version: 2, snapshot }, true],
    [
      "a bootstrap below version 0",
      (raw) => bootstrapEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { version: -1, snapshot },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "a bootstrap between versions",
      (raw) => bootstrapEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { version: 0.5, snapshot },
      false,
    ],
    [
      "a bootstrap with a broken snapshot",
      (raw) => bootstrapEnvelope.parse(raw),
      { version: 0, snapshot: {} },
      false,
    ],
  ];
  const wrong = cases.filter(([, read, raw, takes]) => {
    try {
      read(raw);
      return !takes;
    } catch {
      return takes;
    }
  });
  expect(wrong.map(([name]) => name)).toEqual([]);
});

test("a snapshot keeps the app's own fields beside the stream and revision", () => {

  expect(eventEnvelope.parse(event)).toEqual(event);
});
